title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 4 of lecture notes, apparently taken by Grothendieck at a talk; it is an expository detour on the mod p Steenrod algebra inside the 1976 IHÉS material on the divided-power de Rham complex. In modern language:

(1) Steenrod defined the stable operations P^i. For p = 2 the mod-2 Steenrod algebra is A_2 = F_2<Sq^i, i ≥ 0> / (Sq^0 = 1, Adem relations), with deg Sq^i = i and Sq^1 = β, the Bockstein. An example Adem relation is attempted and marked '(?)'.

(2) Cartan formula: P^i(x×y) = Σ_j P^j(x) P^{i-j}(y).

(3) Monomials P^I = β^{ε0} P^{η1} β^{ε1} P^{η2} ..., with ε_i ∈ {0,1} and η_i ≥ 0. Each has a degree and an excess, the latter given loosely in quotes as η1 − Σ_{i>1} η_i, which is really the p = 2 formula. P^I is admissible when η_i ≥ p η_{i+1} + ε_i. The admissible monomials form an F_p-basis of A (Serre for p = 2, Cartan for odd p).

(4) The evaluation map A → H^*(K(F_p,n), F_p), x ↦ x·ι_n.

(5) Serre–Cartan theorem. H^*(K(F_p,n); F_p) is the free graded-commutative algebra on the P^I ι_n with I admissible of excess < n. Dually, the homology H_*(K(F_p,n); F_p) is a free graded-commutative algebra with divided powers (Cartan).

The point for the course is presumably this last statement: Cartan's divided-power structure on the homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces. The next page computes it via the bar construction / Eilenberg–Moore spectral sequence, or via Serre's fibration method, as a model or motivation for the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: The Adem relation is written Sq^1Sq^2 = Sq^3 + Sq^2Sq^1 with '(?)'. The correct relation is Sq^1Sq^2 = Sq^3; the crossed-out start 'Sq^1Sq^2 = Sq…' was heading toward the right answer. (A genuine two-term example is Sq^2Sq^2 = Sq^3Sq^1.)

The excess formula 'η1 − Σ_{i>1} η_i' is the p = 2 version. For odd p the excess involves 2η1 + ε0 and the degrees of the remaining terms, and Cartan's description needs a slightly more careful excess condition.
The theorem is labelled 'Serre (p=2)' but is stated for F_p in general; the odd-p case is due to Cartan. 'Anticommutative libre' means a polynomial algebra when p = 2.
The homology statement ('générée par les éléments duaux') is vague. Cartan's precise result names specific generators of a free divided-power algebra, not simply duals of the cohomology generators.

ideas.what: Steenrod algebra presented by Sq^i / P^i, β, and the Adem relations
Admissible monomials and excess; admissible monomials form a basis
Cohomology of K(F_p,n) is free graded-commutative on admissible P^I ι_n of excess < n; homology is a free divided-power algebra

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook material on the Steenrod algebra and Serre–Cartan, recorded as lecture notes and containing a small slip in an Adem relation. The link between Cartan's divided powers on Eilenberg–MacLane homology and the divided-power de Rham theme is well known historically.
transcription_corrections: The page number at the bottom left reads 366 (archive foliation), not part of the mathematics.
'p 2' in the middle of the page is likely 'p = 2' or a stray note, not a formula.
In the Cartan formula the sum is over j ≥ 0, and the arguments are P^j(x) P^{i-j}(y), as transcribed.
